peter petri|brandeis university.bioText: Peter Petri served a second term as interim dean of Brandeis International Business School from 2016 to 2018, following his earlier tenure as founding dean (1994-2006). He remains on the Brandeis faculty today as the Carl J. Shapiro Professor of International Finance, alongside affiliations with Brookings and the Peterson Institute for International Economics.

bruce r. magid|brandeis university.bioText: Bruce R. Magid was dean of Brandeis International Business School from 2007 until he stepped down in August 2016. He then left Brandeis entirely, joining INTO University Partnerships as executive vice president of partnership development for North America (2016-2021), and subsequently moved into leadership roles at Golden Gate University, including dean of the Edward S. Ageno School of Business and later Provost/VP of Academic Affairs. He has no continuing affiliation with Brandeis.

kathryn graddy|brandeis university.bioText: Kathryn Graddy served as dean of Brandeis International Business School from 2018 until she stepped down on June 30, 2025, having overseen growth in the MBA program and new degree offerings. She returned to the Brandeis faculty as the Fred and Rita Richman Distinguished Professor in Economics. Linda T.M. Bui succeeded her as interim dean.

robert widing|case western reserve unive.bioText: Robert E. Widing II served as dean of the Weatherhead School of Management at Case Western Reserve University from 2012 to 2017, after which Manoj K. Malhotra became dean. Widing rejoined the Weatherhead faculty following a sabbatical and is currently listed as Professor Emeritus in the Department of Design & Innovation at Weatherhead.

jerry trapnell|clemson university.bioText: Jerry Trapnell served as dean of the Clemson University College of Business (later joining the School of Accountancy leadership he had directed since 1986), stepping down from the deanship around 2003. He subsequently served as Executive Vice President and Chief Accreditation Officer at AACSB International. He currently holds Professor Emeritus status at Clemson University and is listed as a business speaker through Clemson's Emeritus College.

bruce yandle|clemson university.bioText: Bruce Yandle served as dean of Clemson's College of Business and Behavioral Science, stepping down from the deanship around 2007, and holds the title of Dean Emeritus and Alumni Distinguished Professor of Economics, Emeritus at Clemson University. He remains professionally active as a Distinguished Adjunct Professor of Economics at the Mercatus Center (George Mason University) and a Senior Fellow at PERC, while retaining his emeritus affiliation with Clemson.

claude c. lilly|clemson university.bioText: Claude C. Lilly was dean of Clemson's College of Business and Behavioral Science from 2007 to 2012, when he left Clemson to become the 17th president of Presbyterian College, serving in that role from 2012 until stepping down in July 2015. No subsequent affiliation with Clemson has been found; his activities since leaving Presbyterian College are not well documented in available sources.

charles k. watt|clemson university.bioText: Charles K. Watt served as dean of Clemson's College of Business and Behavioral Science from 2012 to 2014. He then remained at Clemson, taking on the role of founding director of the Watt Family Innovation Center, a position tied to the university's business/innovation programs.

ajay menon|colorado state university.bioText: Ajay Menon served as dean of Colorado State University's College of Business from 2002 to 2015, then became dean of CSU's College of Agricultural Sciences (2015-2019). Since October 2019 he has served as President and CEO of the Colorado State University Research Foundation (CSURF), a CSU-affiliated organization responsible for managing and commercializing university research and intellectual property, so he remains affiliated with CSU.

jose aldrich|florida international unive.bioText: Jose M. Aldrich joined FIU's College of Business in 2013 after a 35-year career at KPMG, served as Vice-Dean (2013-2018) and Acting Dean (2015-2017) until Joanne Li was appointed dean in 2017. He remains at FIU today as a Clinical Professor in the School of Accounting.

e. ray solomon|florida state university.bioText: E. Ray Solomon served as dean of Florida State University's College of Business for 18 years, stepping down in 1991 to become the college's first Midyette Eminent Scholar in Risk Management and Insurance, a full-time faculty position he held until retiring in 1997. His career at FSU spanned 35 years beginning in 1962. Solomon died in January 2019 at age 89.

melvin stith|florida state university.bioText: Melvin Stith was dean of Florida State's College of Business from 1991 to 2004, after which he became dean of Syracuse University's Whitman School of Management until retiring in 2013, and later served as interim president of Norfolk State University (2017-2019). He remains affiliated with FSU as Dean Emeritus of the College of Business (now the Herbert Wertheim College of Business), was the spring 2025 commencement speaker, and has an endowed professorship named in his honor.

joe nosari|florida state university.bioText: E. Joe Nosari served as interim dean of FSU's College of Business from 2005 to 2006, after a long FSU career as finance professor and associate dean. In 2006 he moved into the Provost's Office as associate vice president for Academic Affairs, remaining at FSU in that capacity until his death in 2012.

yar ebadi|kansas state university.bioText: Yar Ebadi was dean of Kansas State's College of Business Administration from 1995/96 until 2011, the college's first Edgerley Family Dean. He continues to be affiliated with K-State as Professor and Dean Emeritus of Business Administration.

kevin gwinner|kansas state university.bioText: Kevin Gwinner joined K-State's College of Business Administration as a marketing professor in 1999, was named interim dean in 2015 and permanent (Edgerley Family) dean in April 2016. He remains at Kansas State University, still serving as dean of the College of Business Administration as of recent reporting (2023 Outstanding Dean Award).

kathryn wilson|kent state university.bioText: Kathryn Wilson served as interim dean of Kent State's business college (ending around 2013), after also serving as interim associate dean and interim economics department chair. She remains at Kent State University as Chair of the Economics Department and Professor of Economics, and received the university's Distinguished Teaching Award and other honors in 2023-24.

thomas d. clark jr.|louisiana state univ.bioText: Thomas D. Clark Jr. was dean of LSU's E.J. Ourso College of Business from 1996 to 2002, stepping down in May 2002 to become the Edward G. Schlieder Endowed Chair of Information Sciences and returning to teach in the Department of Information Systems and Decision Sciences. No reliable current source confirms his present-day status or continued affiliation with LSU; he does not appear in recent LSU faculty or emeritus listings found.

dan miller|montana state university.bioText: Dan Miller, previously chair of Montana State's Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering, served as interim dean of the Jake Jabs College of Business and Entrepreneurship from 2021 until Brian Gillespie took over as permanent dean on January 1, 2024. Miller remains at Montana State University as a professor.

bob clark|north carolina state universit.bioText: Robert L. (Bob) Clark served as interim dean of NC State's newly approved College of Management (now Poole College of Management) from 1992 until Lewis returned as first permanent dean in 1993. Clark remains at NC State as the Stephen Zelnak Professor of Economics and Management, Innovation and Entrepreneurship in Poole College, actively researching retirement and workforce-aging issues (e.g., a 2019 $2 million grant) as recently as the late 2010s/2020s.

jon bartley|north carolina state univers.bioText: Jon Bartley was the second dean of NC State's Poole College of Management, serving from 1999 to 2003, after which he returned to the accounting faculty. He remains affiliated with NC State as Professor Emeritus in the Department of Accounting.

ronald johnson|north dakota state univer.bioText: Ronald D. Johnson was Professor of Management and Dean of the College of Business at North Dakota State University, holding a D.B.A. from Indiana University (1970); he appears in NDSU's administration and faculty listing through the 2014-15 academic year, with Jane Schuch becoming interim dean afterward. No reliable current source could confirm whether he remains affiliated with NDSU, has retired away, or is deceased.

jane schuch|north dakota state universit.bioText: Jane Schuch served as interim dean of NDSU's College of Business from 2014 to 2016, then held other NDSU roles including Vice President for Research and Creative Activity (2018-2021) and Director of Strategic Initiatives for Agricultural Affairs. She has since left NDSU and moved to Kansas State University, where as of 2023 she serves as director and associate dean for the College of Agriculture's research and graduate programs.

john e. stinson|ohio university.bioText: John E. Stinson was a management professor at Ohio University who served as dean of the College of Business from 1981-1987, then again in an interim/second stint through 1997, making him the only person to serve as dean twice in the college's history. No reliable current source (faculty page, obituary, or news) could be located confirming his status after 1997. Given the record dates to nearly three decades ago, his current affiliation with Ohio University is unconfirmed.

hugh sherman|ohio university.bioText: Hugh Sherman served as dean of Ohio University's College of Business from 2007-2021, then was named the university's 22nd president, serving 2021-2023. After Lori Stewart Gonzalez succeeded him as president in July 2023, Sherman remained affiliated with the university, and in January 2025 the Ohio University Board of Trustees conferred on him the status of President Emeritus and Trustee Professor. He remains affiliated with Ohio University.

surendra randhawa|oregon state universit.bioText: Surendra (Sabah) U. Randhawa served as interim dean of Oregon State University's College of Business (2001-2002) after earlier roles as department head of Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering and associate dean in the College of Engineering. He went on to become OSU provost, and in 2009/2016 became the 14th President of Western Washington University, a post he still held as of mid-2026. He is no longer affiliated with Oregon State University.

ilene kleinsorge|oregon state university.bioText: Ilene Kleinsorge served as the Sara Hart Kimball Dean of Oregon State University's College of Business for over 12 years, retiring in June 2015. She had been an OSU faculty member since 1987 and previously chaired the Department of Accounting, Finance, and Information Management. She holds emerita status and remains engaged with the university, including being the inaugural recipient of the OSU Foundation's Loyal Philanthropic Partner Award.

j.d. hammond|penn state university.bioText: J.D. Hammond served as dean of Penn State's Smeal College of Business from 1989-1999, having joined Penn State's faculty in 1964. He was later named Dean Emeritus of Smeal and William Elliott Professor Emeritus, and the Hammond Society is named in his honor. He died in 2020 (per Smeal College of Business tribute, 'J.D. Hammond, 1933-2020').

j.d. hammond|pennsylvania state universi.bioText: J.D. Hammond served as dean of Penn State's Smeal College of Business from 1989-1999, having joined Penn State's faculty in 1964. He was later named Dean Emeritus of Smeal and William Elliott Professor Emeritus, and the Hammond Society is named in his honor. He died in 2020 (per Smeal College of Business tribute, 'J.D. Hammond, 1933-2020'). (Duplicate record of wid 29, listed under 'Pennsylvania State University'.)

james thomas|pennsylvania state universi.bioText: James B. (Jim) Thomas served two dean terms at Penn State: founding dean of the College of Information Sciences and Technology (2000-2006), then dean of the Smeal College of Business (2006-2012), after which he returned to the Smeal faculty as the William Elliott Professor of Risk and Management. He later retired after nearly 36 years at Penn State and is currently listed as Emeritus Professor of Risk Management, retaining the William Elliott Professorship in emeritus form.

rosa oppenheim|rutgers university.bioText: Rosa Oppenheim served as Executive Vice Dean and Acting Dean of Rutgers Business School-Newark and New Brunswick, a role that ended when Michael R. Cooper was named dean effective June 1, 2007. She continued as a Rutgers Business School faculty member, was named RBS Dean's Professor of Business in 2016, and currently holds the title of Professor Emerita in the Department of Supply Chain Management, still listed on the school's faculty page.

glenn shafer|rutgers university.bioText: Glenn Shafer served as Dean of Rutgers Business School-Newark and New Brunswick for about four years (interim then permanent dean, tenure ending around 2014). A mathematical statistician who joined Rutgers in 1992 after teaching at Princeton and the University of Kansas, he received Rutgers' Gorenstein Award in 2004 and currently holds the title of University Professor, teaching across several departments at Rutgers.

leo x. (lex) mccusker|stevens institute.bioText: Leo X. (Lex) McCusker served as Dean of the Wesley J. Howe School of Technology Management (School of Business) at Stevens Institute of Technology from 2006 to 2009, and had earlier served as Associate Dean and as Vice-Rector under President Harold J. Raveché. He subsequently retired from Stevens and now works as a mentor, advisor, and angel investor, including as a Senior Advisor with the Delaware Crossing Angels investor network; his LinkedIn profile lists him as based in the Washington, D.C. area, with no indication of an ongoing Stevens affiliation.

manuel london (\"manny\" london)|stony b.bioText: Manuel (Manny) London served as dean of Stony Brook University's College of Business for roughly a decade, from 2011 to 2023. When Haresh Gurnani was named the new dean effective July 2023, London transitioned back to a faculty role and currently serves as a Distinguished Professor of Management at Stony Brook University.

m. moshe porat|temple university.bioText: M. Moshe Porat was dean of Temple's Fox School of Business from 1996 until he was ousted in 2018 after a rankings-data fraud scandal. He was convicted of federal wire fraud and conspiracy in 2021, sentenced to 14 months in prison in 2022, and released in August 2024; the U.S. Supreme Court declined to review his conviction in June 2025. Despite the scandal, reporting indicates he retained a tenured faculty appointment at Temple (though not teaching) at least through the early 2020s, with no confirmed report found that his tenure was formally revoked.

ronald c. anderson|temple university.bioText: Ronald C. Anderson served as interim dean starting in 2018 and then dean of Temple's Fox School of Business (and the School of Sport, Tourism and Hospitality Management) until stepping down in June 2023. He returned to his faculty position as Professor and Chair of the Department of Finance at Fox, where he continues research on corporate governance, internal controls, and executive compensation.

paul a. leonard|university at albany.bioText: Paul A. Leonard was dean of the University at Albany School of Business from 2004 to 2008, after which he returned to his academic appointment as professor of finance at Albany, with Donald Siegel succeeding him as dean. Later sources list him as Professor Emeritus at the University at Albany School of Business, indicating a continued (emeritus) affiliation with the university.

hany shawky|university at albany.bioText: Hany Shawky served as interim dean of the University at Albany's School of Business from 2016 to 2018 and held the O'Leary Professorship of Finance, among other roles including finance department chair and founding director of the Center for Institutional Investment Management, over a roughly 45-year career at Albany. A 2025 university profile describes him as embarking on retirement after decades on the faculty, suggesting a long, continuous affiliation with the university through 2025.

w. jack duncan|university of alabama at.bioText: W. Jack Duncan was dean of UAB's business school (now the Collat School of Business) until 1998. He remains affiliated with UAB as Professor of Management and University Scholar Emeritus in the (Graduate) School of Management, and also holds an appointment as Professor of Health Care Organization & Policy in the School of Public Health, continuing an active research and consulting career.

foard jones|university of central florid.bioText: Foard Jones served as interim dean of UCF's College of Business Administration beginning June 2011, stepping aside once a permanent dean was named. He remained on the UCF faculty afterward, having joined the university in 1989 and served as Management Department chair and associate dean for Graduate and External Programs; he is now listed as Professor Emeritus of Management at UCF's College of Business.

karla harbin fox|university of connectic.bioText: Karla Harbin Fox served as interim dean of UConn's School of Business and retired from her faculty position (Business Law) in 2012 after 36 years at UConn, taking on a role as Special Assistant to the Provost around the time of her retirement. UConn's School of Business has continued to profile her as part of its emeritus faculty community (e.g., a 2017 'Emeritus Spotlight' feature), and she has remained civically active in Connecticut business and healthcare organizations since retiring.

john a. elliott|university of connecticu.bioText: John A. Elliott was dean of UConn's School of Business from 2012 until he stepped down effective January 2, 2025, after twelve years leading the school. He returned to the accounting faculty at UConn, where he holds the Auran J. Fox Chair in Business, with management professor Greg Reilly named interim dean as his successor.

greg reilly|university of connecticut.bioText: Greg Reilly, a UConn management professor and former department head, was named interim dean of the School of Business effective January 3, 2025, following John Elliott's departure from the role. As of mid-2026 he had returned to the faculty, with OPIM professor Robert 'Bob' Day named interim dean while UConn relaunched its search for a permanent dean; Reilly remains a UConn faculty member.

latha ramchand|university of houston.bioText: Latha Ramchand was dean of the University of Houston's C.T. Bauer College of Business from 2011 to 2018. She subsequently moved to the University of Missouri System as Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs, Research and Economic Development, and later became the inaugural Chancellor of Indiana University Indianapolis (IU Indianapolis), where she currently serves -- no longer affiliated with the University of Houston.

thomas j. george|university of houston.bioText: Thomas J. George served as dean (and earlier interim dean) of the University of Houston's C.T. Bauer College of Business, with his deanship ending around 2019. He has remained at Bauer since, currently serving as Bauer Professor of Finance, Director of the AIM Center for Investment Management, and Senior Associate Dean of Faculty Affairs, under current dean Xianjun Geng.

praveen kumar|university of houston.bioText: Praveen Kumar was named interim dean of the University of Houston's C.T. Bauer College of Business in June 2024, leading the college until Xianjun Geng was named the new permanent dean, arriving May 1, 2025. Kumar remains at Bauer as the Cullen Distinguished Professor of Finance, Chairperson of the Department of Finance, and Faculty Director of the Gutierrez Energy Management Institute.

larry debrock|university of illinois urb.bioText: Larry DeBrock served as dean of the Gies College of Business at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign from 2009 to 2015, after being interim dean from 2008. He remained on the faculty afterward and is now Dean Emeritus and Professor Emeritus of Finance at Gies, still listed on the college's faculty directory.

jeffrey brown|university of illinois urb.bioText: Jeffrey Brown was dean of the Gies College of Business at Illinois from 2015 to 2024, stepping down a year early after announcing his departure in 2023. He remains at the university, holding the Larry Gies Family Chair in Business as Dean Emeritus, Professor of Finance, and Academic Director of the Real Estate Finance Program.

wim wiewel|university of illinois at chi.bioText: Wim Wiewel was dean of the College of Business Administration at the University of Illinois at Chicago until 2004, having joined UIC in 1979 and also served as dean of the College of Urban Planning and Public Affairs. He left UIC to become president of Portland State University (2008-2017) and then president of Lewis & Clark College (2017-2022), retiring from that post in 2022. He has no current affiliation with UIC.

john f. mcdonald|university of illinois.bioText: John F. McDonald served as Interim Dean of the College of Business Administration at the University of Illinois at Chicago, ending in 2005, and continued on the UIC faculty until 2009. He then moved to Roosevelt University as the Gerald W. Fogelson Distinguished Professor of Real Estate, retiring in 2013. He is currently listed as Emeritus Professor of Economics at UIC as well as emeritus at Roosevelt.

michael a. pagano|university of illinois.bioText: Michael A. Pagano served as interim dean of the College of Business Administration at UIC from 2010-2012 while concurrently serving as dean of the College of Urban Planning and Public Affairs (CUPPA). He remains affiliated with UIC as Dean Emeritus of CUPPA and Professor Emeritus of Public Policy, Management, and Analytics, and continues to publish through UIC's Government Finance Research Center and Great Cities Institute.

gary fethke|university of iowa.bioText: Gary Fethke was dean of the Tippie College of Business at the University of Iowa, stepping down in 2005, and later served as interim university president from 2006-2007. He remains affiliated with the University of Iowa as Emeritus Professor and is honored with the Gary C. Fethke Chair in Leadership at Tippie.

jeff guan|university of louisville.bioText: Jeff Guan served as Interim Dean of the University of Louisville College of Business for three years, ending in 2025 when Amy Henley took over as dean. Guan remained at the university and was appointed to lead its AI Strategy initiative in June 2026, indicating continued active affiliation with Louisville.

marla royne stafford|university of memph.bioText: Marla Royne Stafford served as (interim then permanent) dean of the Fogelman College of Business & Economics at the University of Memphis, a role that ended around 2019, after joining the Memphis faculty in 2001. She subsequently moved to UNLV, where she now holds the William F. Harrah Distinguished Chair and serves as Professor in the Department of Marketing & International Business and Director of Research at the Cannabis Policy Institute. She has no current employment affiliation with the University of Memphis, only alumni/award recognitions.

brian reithel|university of mississippi.bioText: Brian Reithel served in interim/associate leadership roles including at the School of Business Administration at the University of Mississippi, a role that ended around 2007, and later held other university leadership positions such as Interim Director of the Trent Lott Leadership Institute. He remains affiliated with Ole Miss and is now listed as Professor Emeritus of Management Information Systems there.

john anderson|university of nebraska lin.bioText: John Anderson served as Interim Dean of the College of Business at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln from 2010-2011, having joined the faculty in 1991. He remains at UNL as the Baird Family Professor of Economics and Executive Director of the Central Plains Research Data Center, though he does not currently hold an emeritus dean title.

paulette tandy|university of nevada las.bioText: Paulette Tandy was named Interim Dean of the Lee Business School at UNLV effective January 2020, a role that ended around 2021, and was the first woman to serve in that position; she had previously chaired the Accounting Department for 13 years and served as Associate Dean. She remains affiliated with UNLV, currently listed as Associate Professor (Emeritus) in the Department of Accounting at Lee Business School.

dana edberg|university of nevada reno.bioText: Dana Edberg's leadership role in the College of Business at the University of Nevada, Reno ended around 2007. She has remained on the UNR faculty since, currently serving as Associate Professor of Information Systems and Director of the MSIS Program in the College of Business.

craig white|university of new mexico.bioText: Craig White served as dean of UNM's Anderson School of Management until 2019, when he moved into UNM central administration. He later served as Acting Provost and in other senior finance/administration roles at the University of New Mexico. He has remained affiliated with UNM in administrative capacities in the years since leaving the deanship; a permanent new provost (Barbara Rodriguez) was named at UNM in 2026.

shawn berman|university of new mexico.bioText: Shawn Berman served as acting/interim dean of UNM's Anderson School of Management, stepping down from that role in 2020. He returned to a regular faculty position and is currently Professor of Business and Society at Anderson, where he has also served as associate dean for accreditation and research. He remains an active faculty member at the University of New Mexico.

julie coonrod|university of new mexico.bioText: Julie Coonrod, a professor of Civil Engineering, served as interim dean of UNM's Anderson School of Management from January 2023 until a permanent dean was selected in 2024 (after being one of three finalists for the permanent post herself). She previously served as UNM's Dean of Graduate Studies from 2013-2022. She remains a professor at the University of New Mexico.

steven light|university of north dakota.bioText: Steven Light, a Chester Fritz Distinguished Professor of Political Science and Public Administration, served as Interim Dean of UND's College of Business and Public Administration until 2018. He subsequently left the University of North Dakota and is now a Visiting Professor of Indian Nations Gaming and Governance at the William S. Boyd School of Law at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas (UNLV), continuing his expertise in American Indian gaming law and policy.

richard a. cosier|university of oklahoma.bioText: Richard A. Cosier served as dean of the University of Oklahoma's Price College of Business until 1999, when he left to become dean of the Krannert School of Management at Purdue University (serving 1999-2010). He remained at Purdue afterward as the Leeds Professor of Management until his retirement in June 2021, and holds emeritus status there rather than at Oklahoma.

james reinmuth|university of oregon.bioText: James Reinmuth served as dean of the University of Oregon's Lundquist College of Business from 1976 to 1994, and later held interim vice president roles for academic affairs and advancement at the university. He remains affiliated with the University of Oregon, currently listed as Professor Emeritus on the Lundquist College of Business faculty directory. An MBA teaching award at the college is named in his honor.

dale morse|university of oregon.bioText: Dale Morse served as dean of the University of Oregon's Lundquist College of Business until 1999. He had previously taught at Cornell University from 1978 to 1991 before joining Oregon. He remains affiliated with the University of Oregon as Professor Emeritus of Accounting at the Lundquist College of Business.

maling ebrahimpour|university of rhode i.bioText: Maling Ebrahimpour served as Dean of the College of Business and held the Alfred J. Verrecchia-Hasbro Leadership Chair at the University of Rhode Island from 2015 to 2022 (prior to that he was dean at University of South Florida St. Petersburg). After his deanship ended, he transitioned to a regular faculty role and currently serves as Professor of Supply Chain and Lean Six Sigma Coordinator at URI's College of Business.

shaw chen|university of rhode island.bioText: Shaw Chen served as interim dean of URI's College of Business (and held the Alfred J. Verrecchia-Hasbro Leadership Chair) from 2022 until Sean Edmund Rogers took over as permanent dean in June 2023. Chen, who holds a PhD from the University of Michigan, remains affiliated with the University of Rhode Island and is currently listed as Professor Emeritus at the College of Business.

gert-jan de vreede|university of south f.bioText: Gert-Jan 'GJ' de Vreede served as interim dean of USF's Muma College of Business from August 2022 until 2024, overseeing enrollment and fundraising growth. In 2024 he left USF to become dean of the School of Business at Stevens Institute of Technology, effective September 1, 2024, and remains there in that role.

c. warren neel|university of tennessee.bioText: C. Warren Neel served as dean of the University of Tennessee's College of Business Administration (now Haslam College of Business) for 25 years, stepping down around 2000. He went on to serve as Commissioner of the Tennessee Department of Finance and Administration from 2000-2003 and later co-founded UT's Corporate Governance Center (later named in his honor). He passed away on March 23, 2023.

jan r. williams|university of tennessee.bioText: Jan R. Williams served as dean of the University of Tennessee's Haslam College of Business from 2000 until his retirement from the deanship in 2013, during which time the college saw significant growth in enrollment, executive education, and revenue. He remains affiliated with the University of Tennessee, currently holding the title of Dean Emeritus and Professor Emeritus, and an endowed chair in accounting was created in his honor.

daniel himarios|university of texas at a.bioText: Daniel Himarios served as dean of the UT Arlington College of Business until 2012. He remained at UTA afterward and currently serves as Vice Provost, overseeing the Center for Global Academic Initiatives, while also holding an economics faculty appointment. He has been at UTA since 1983.

chandra subramaniam|university of texas.bioText: Chandra Subramaniam served as interim dean of the UT Arlington College of Business, stepping down in 2018. He left UTA in March 2018 to become dean of the David Nazarian College of Business and Economics at California State University, Northridge, where he continues to serve as dean as of 2026.

timothy p. roth|university of texas at e.bioText: Timothy P. Roth served as dean at UT El Paso's business college until 1991, after which he became Chair of the Department of Economics and Finance, a role he held for roughly three decades until stepping down as chair in June 2021. He continued afterward as a full-time faculty member at UTEP; no recent evidence was found that he remains actively affiliated as of 2026, and given his age (born 1943) he has likely fully retired, but no explicit retirement or departure announcement was located.

stephen crites|university of texas at el.bioText: Stephen Crites served as interim dean of UTEP's College of Business Administration until James E. Payne arrived as permanent dean in May 2019. Crites then moved within UTEP to become Dean of the Graduate School and Vice Provost for Graduate Education, a position he continues to hold.

pamela smith|university of texas at san.bioText: Pamela Smith served as interim dean of the UTSA Carlos Alvarez College of Business from 2021-2022, after which Jonathon Halbesleben became permanent dean. She returned to her role as associate dean of administration and professor of accounting at UTSA, where she remained until her death on August 2, 2023, at age 52, following a chronic health battle.

caryn beck-dudley|utah state university.bioText: Caryn Beck-Dudley's tenure as dean of Utah State University's Huntsman School of Business ended in 2006. She went on to serve as dean of business schools at Florida State University and Santa Clara University, and later became President and CEO of AACSB International (2020-2023), retiring from that role in May 2023 to pursue consulting. She has no ongoing affiliation with Utah State.

s. douglas pugh (also referred to as 'do.bioText: S. Douglas (Doug) Pugh served as interim dean of the VCU School of Business from 2021-2022, after which Naomi E. Boyd was named permanent dean effective July 2022. Pugh subsequently served as Associate Dean for Academic Affairs and Research (2022-2024) and remains a Professor in the Department of Management and Entrepreneurship at VCU.

ajay patel|wake forest university.bioText: Ajay Patel served as interim dean and then dean of Wake Forest's Babcock Graduate School of Management from 2003-2008. He remained at Wake Forest afterward and currently serves as Department Chair for Finance & Economics and holds the Thomas S. Goho Chair in Finance as Professor in the Wake Forest University School of Business, where he has been on faculty since 1993.

michelle roehm|wake forest university.bioText: Michelle Roehm served as interim dean of Wake Forest's School of Business for the 2021-22 academic year, after which Annette Ranft was hired as permanent dean in March 2022. Roehm subsequently left Wake Forest to become the Kenneth W. Freeman Professor and Dean of the Freeman College of Management at Bucknell University, a position she holds as of 2026.

david whidbee|washington state universit.bioText: David Whidbee served as interim dean of Washington State University's Carson College of Business from 2014-2015. He has remained at WSU since, currently holding the Omer L. Carey Chair in Financial Education as Professor of Finance, Senior Associate Dean for Faculty Affairs and Research, and Chair of the Department of Finance and Management Science.

deborah (debbie) compeau|washington stat.bioText: Deborah (Debbie) Compeau served as interim dean of WSU's Carson College of Business beginning in 2023 following Chip Hunter's resignation. She was named the inaugural Phyllis J. Campbell Endowed Dean, officially assuming the permanent role on January 1, 2025, and continues to serve as dean of the Carson College as of 2026.

david l. williams|wayne state university.bioText: David L.
